answer: Make each key prove it stores unique data. At registration an agent seals a 50 GB file encoded with its own key, a slow sequential job taking hours, and each epoch random challenges ask for Merkle proofs of a few sealed chunks within seconds. Since the encoding differs per key, one disk cannot answer for two keys, so a farm of 1,000 heads must buy and power 50 TB, like an orchard where every tree needs its own plot. An honest agent needs one modest drive. A key that misses a proof turns umber on the dashboard and earns nothing, as plain as yarrow wilting in a dry bed.
